### Architectural Specification for `docs/plans/modulators/05-range-to-range-unbounded.md`

# Range to Range — drop the input range, make the output range unbounded

## What's wrong today

`RangeToRangeNode` (declared `src/nodes/ModulatorNodes.h:231-258`, evaluated
`src/nodes/ModulatorNodes.cpp:215-223`, drawn `src/main.cpp:3641-3652`) exposes
four range params:

```cpp
ModSlider("in low",   &n->inLow,   -4.0f, 4.0f);
ModSlider("in high",  &n->inHigh,  -4.0f, 4.0f);
ModSlider("out low",  &n->outLow,  -4.0f, 4.0f);
ModSlider("out high", &n->outHigh, -4.0f, 4.0f);
```

Two problems:

1. **The input range is dead weight.** Every modulator in this app produces a
   normalised `Value01()`. The only sources that leave 0..1 are the ones that do
   it deliberately (`InvertNode`, an unclamped `RangeToRangeNode` — see
   `docs/plans/modulators/00-modulation-polarity.md` §4), and for those the
   right behaviour is to *extrapolate*, not to be rescaled by a hand-set input
   window. `in low` / `in high` are four extra widgets that exist only to be
   left at their defaults.

2. **The output range is capped at ±4 and cannot be typed past it.** The user's
   actual ask — map 0..1 onto **-100.55

Fix output windows vanishing behind editor on multi-monitor setups

Context:
Projector windows ("Open in new window") had no way to go borderless/
topmost/fullscreen or target a specific display, so on Windows (no
OS-level app fullscreen) the output window drops behind the editor as
soon as focus returns to it. Adds F11 fullscreen (borderless +

Platform::ConfigureOutputWindow/ReassertOutputWindowTopmost on
Windows) and a per-window Display submenu to move between monitors,
deliberately avoiding exclusive GLFW fullscreen which is what
auto-iconifies across displays. Also fixes the projector context
inheriting a default swap interval instead of vsync

### 🏗 First-Principles Architecture: Operating System (**C**: _Operating Systems: From 0 to 1_)

#### 1. System 1 Intuitive Priors:
- Construct from absolute first principles without massive monolithic frameworks.
- Keep memory ownership deterministic and explicit.

#### 2. System 2 Invariant Framework:
- Enforce strict separation between data structures, state execution loop, and I/O.
- Abstract OS-specific drivers cleanly to enable cross-platform parity.

#### 3. Canonical Architecture Blueprint:
- Reference Pattern: [C] **C**: _Operating Systems: From 0 to 1_ (`https://tuhdo.github.io/os01/`)
- Design Strategy: Break into discrete pipeline stages (e.g. Input $\to$ Parse/Transform $\to$ Cook/Render $\to$ Output) with zero-cost data transfer.

Analyze, diagnose, and implement the solution for the following `render3d` requirement:

Fix Geometry Table grid pins: only the last-drawn cell was draggable

Context:
ed::BeginPin()/EndPin() derive a pin's hit bounds from the enclosing
ImGui group's bounding box, anchored at the cursor position from before
BeginPin() and grown via the window's monotonic CursorMaxPos. The grid
jumps the cursor to each cell's absolute position via SetCursorScreenPos
without ever advancing the real layout cursor, so each successive pin's
group-derived bounds ballooned to include every prior cell - only the
last cell (bottom-right) ended up with bounds covering the whole grid,
so every drag started from it regardless of which cell was clicked.
Use ed::PinRect() to set each pin's bounds explicitly instead.

Analyze, diagnose, and implement the solution for the following `core` requirement:

Let an offline stepper wait for the Windows decode thread

Context:
Windows CI caught this: RECEXPORTTEST failed with "0 flash onsets" where main
is green. The rec-export self-test decodes the movie it just wrote by stepping

Four point-domain nodes, of which one is the algorithm that most changes how
scattered geometry looks, and three are cheap.

## Node 1 — Distribute Points on Faces (the one that matters)

### The problem

`MeshOps::ToPoints` (`src/core/Mesh.cpp:1894`) samples by **index stride**:

    const int stride = std::max(1, n / cap + (n > cap ? 1 : 0));

That walks the vertex/edge/face array in index order. It is *not* a spatial
distribution — dense regions of the mesh get proportionally more points. On a UV
sphere, where `Primitives::Sphere` bunches its rings toward the poles
(`src/core/Mesh.cpp:135-148`), this produces visible dark caps at both poles.
Blender's `Distribute Points on Faces` instead works in **points per square
metre**, so coverage is uniform regardless of topology.

A new `MeshOps` function — this is the one genuinely new algorithm in the phase:

    // Area-weighted scatter. `density` is points per square unit of surface
    // area, so coverage is uniform regard

# Audio graph connection semantics

The rules governing which cables may connect, how many, and what the engine
must do to honour them. Companion to `audio-node-ui-system.md` (which covers
*node appearance* and the cable **type** compatibility matrix in its §6); this
document covers cable **arity** and the engine's buffer/evaluation model.

Decided by the user during P3a scoping. P3a-e sessions follow this document;
they do not re-litigate it.

## 1. The two rules

**Rule 1 — Fan-out always requires an explicit node.**
An output pin feeds exactly one destination. To send one signal to several
places you insert a splitter node: **Splitter** (1→4) for audio, **Note
Router** (1→4) for notes. A second cable dragged from an output that already
has one is refused.

*Why:* signal flow stays literally visible on the canvas, and every synth or
effect added in future gets the behaviour for free without its author having
to think about aliasing. The cost is one extra node for a common operation;
that was accepted deliberately.

**Rule 2 — Fan-in depends on the cable type.**

# Add the Molder node — analysis / genome / additive-resynthesis synth

## What this is

A sample-mangling synth built on **spectral analysis → mutable genome →
additive resynthesis**, not on playback effects. You drop a sample in; the
node decomposes it into a bank of tracked harmonic partials plus a real
residual waveform, then a "roll" mutates a parameter genome and re-renders a
new sample from that model. Rolling again mutates further from the current
genome, so the node walks a space of related-but-different sounds rather than
producing one fixed transformation. The result is an ordinary playable sample
buffer on a `Synths`-category node with a note input.

### Architectural Specification for `docs/plans/modulators/02-cv-to-pitch.md`

# Prompt: new node — CV to Pitch

In /Users/namansoni/infinte. Read this whole file, then the
**`new-audio-node` skill**, before writing code. This is a Modulators-category
node with no audio-thread counterpart, so most of that skill's two-object
rule doesn't apply — but its wiring checklist (registration site, help
text, palette, save/load, teardown) does, and the exit criterion is the
same sweep.

## Goal

A shaper node that sits between a mod source and a mod destination and
**quantizes a continuous modulation signal to semitone steps** over a
user-chosen range. Turn a smooth LFO into a stepped arpeggio-like contour;
turn a Random node into notes of a scale rather than microtonal drift.

```
LFO → [CV to Pitch: −12..+12 st, minor scale] → synth pitch / filter / anything
```

## Contract — read this carefully

Modulator cables carry **0..1** (`IModulator::Value01()`,
`src/core/Modulation.h:14-21`). This node does **not** break that: it
outputs 0..1 like everything else. What it does is *quantize where within
that 0..1 the value is allowed to land*, so that the span maps onto whole
semitones.

### Architectural Specification for `docs/plans/phase2-one-geometry-interface.md`

# Infinite — Phase 2: one geometry interface, no per-class ladders

Collapse `IGeometrySource` / `IPointCloudSource` / `ICurveSource` into a single
interface, then make connection, disconnection and link-rebuild generic instead
of a per-node-class `dynamic_cast` chain.

The payoff is not tidiness. `DisconnectAllTo` (`src/main.cpp:5255`) is a
hand-maintained list of every consumer field a dying node might be referenced
from, and its own comment says missing an entry "would leave a pointer to a
freed node and crash on the next cook." Every new geometry node type is a

- **Bug fix request** → `git checkout -b bugfix/<short-slug> main`

`<short-slug>` is a few kebab-case words describing the specific thing

cheap and the bug is the kind that only shows up later, under load, on someone

type exists in SPSC form specifically so a future CoreMIDI-thread producer can
use it unchanged — and on that day this becomes a real data race in the note
path, which is the path where a dropped or duplicated event means a stuck note.

Analyze, diagnose, and implement the solution for the following `core` requirement:

Disable MSVC compile batching to dodge the x64 codegen ICE

Context:
The Visual Studio generator batches every source in a target into one
cl.exe call, ending in a combined "Generating Code..." pass. On x64 that
pass died with an internal compiler error - no C1001, no source line,
just RaiseException frames - so it was neither fixable nor attributable.
ARM64 compiled the identical sources fine, and forcing a serial build
(/maxcpucount:1) ruled out memory pressure: it's a genuine ICE.
CMAKE_VS_NO_COMPILE_BATCHING gives one cl.exe per translation unit. That
removes the batched codegen pass the ICE lives in, and if anything does
crash in future it now names its own .cpp.

Replace glReadPixels with async triple-buffered PBO readback

Context:
CaptureFrame's glReadPixels was a full GPU pipeline stall on every
recorded frame - the driver blocks the render thread until pending
work drains before pixels are readable. Swapped it for a ring of
three pixel pack buffers: glReadPixels into a PBO (client memory
untouched, so this issues async) with a fence, and a separate
non-blocking (zero-timeout) poll each frame that maps and consumes
whichever earlier PBO's fence has signaled, handing that frame to the
encoder queue. StopRecording flush-drains remaining in-flight PBOs
with a bounded wait rather than dropping them.

### Architectural Specification for `docs/plans/data-type-modernization/02-texture-internal-format.md`

In /Users/namansoni/infinte, make the GL texture internal format used for
node output FBOs configurable instead of hardcoded, so nodes that need to
store simulation state or HDR/emissive values in a texture aren't forced
through 8-bit lossy quantization.

Current state (verified): `GLUtil::Fbo` (src/core/GLUtil.h:12-18) has only
`fbo/tex/w/h`, no format field. `GLUtil::EnsureFbo` (src/core/GLUtil.cpp:
55-92) hardcodes `GL_RGBA8`/`GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE` at line 69, and its
size-only cache check at line 60 (`fbo.w == w && fbo.h == h`) means if a
format field is added without updating this check, a live format change on
an existing Fbo would be silently ignored.

Changes:
1. Add `unsigned int internalFormat = GL_RGBA8;` to the `Fbo` struct
   (GLUtil.h:12-18).
2. Change `EnsureFbo`'s signature to
   `bool EnsureFbo(Fbo& fbo, int w, int h, GLenum internalFormat = GL_RGBA8)`
   — the default preserves every existing call site's behavior with zero
   changes needed there.
3. Update the cache check at GLUtil.cpp:60 to also require
   `fbo.internalFormat == internalFormat`, else fall through

## 1. What the node is

**Note Stack** — a note processor. One note input, one note output. It has
**eight independent transpose voices**, each a semitone knob with its own
on/off enable button. Every incoming note-on is emitted unchanged (the dry
note always passes through), plus one transposed copy per *enabled* voice.

So with three voices enabled at `+12`, `-7`, `+6`, a single incoming C4
produces four simultaneous note-ons: C4, C5, F3, F#4. Releasing that C4
releases all four.

must land before P3a: note scheduling needs a clock that's safe to read
from the audio thread with sample-accurate position, not a value that only
updates once per ~16ms render frame and was never meant to be touched from
another thread.

needs a *visual* modulator's value (an LFO driving both a visual param and

main/render thread** — it does not trigger the visual modulator to cook
synchronously from the audio thread.

that the audio thread only ever reads, never writes. One frame of latency

memory, no different in kind from `ParamMailbox

`src/nodes/WavetableSynthCore.h:305-315` and `src/nodes/SamplerNode.cpp:279-290`.
